  "raw_idea": "Multi‑hop question answering often relies on reasoning over a chain of facts in a knowledge graph, yet current language‑model training typically uses isolated head‑relation‑tail triples, depriving the model of the surrounding context that supports multi‑step inference. We propose to enrich each target triple (or path) with additional triples drawn from the same source passage, forming a local context subgraph that is presented together with the primary supervision signal. The model will be fine‑tuned under two regimes: one using only the target triple/path and another that also incorporates the supporting context. To improve the reliability of the base facts, we will introduce an adaptive repair loop that detects one‑hop failures, generates corrective examples, and iteratively refines the model. After this cleaning stage, we will apply reinforcement‑learning‑based optimization on lower‑hop QA instances and evaluate transfer to deeper multi‑hop queries.",

input.problem: Language-model and KGQA training typically supervises individual head-relation-tail triples (or a single reasoning path) in isolation. This strips away the surrounding passage context — the co-occurring triples that constrain and disambiguate each fact — which multi-step inference appears to need, and it propagates noisy/incorrect base facts into every downstream hop of a reasoning chain.
input.target_domain: Knowledge-graph question answering (multi-hop reasoning over a knowledge graph), with language models as the reader/reasoner.
input.target_system: An instruction-tuned / fine-tuned language model that answers natural-language questions over a knowledge graph whose triples retain provenance to a source passage (and, for comparison, a graph-neural KGQA model such as those evaluated on WebQSP/CWQ).
input.proposed_method: For each target triple or gold reasoning path, retrieve the additional triples co-occurring in the same source passage to form a local context subgraph, and present that subgraph together with the primary supervision signal. Fine-tune under two matched regimes (isolated triple/path vs. triple/path + local context subgraph). Add an adaptive repair loop that detects one-hop failures, generates corrective training examples, and iteratively refines the model. Then apply RL-based optimization on lower-hop QA instances and measure transfer to deeper multi-hop queries.
input.hypothesis: Augmenting isolated triple/path supervision with a co-passage local context subgraph improves multi-hop QA accuracy and, specifically, generalization to deeper-hop queries compared with the isolated-supervision baseline; an adaptive one-hop-failure repair loop over noisy base facts yields further, measurable gains in answer reliability.
input.research_question: Does augmenting isolated triple/path supervision with a co-passage local context subgraph improve multi-hop KG question answering and generalization to deeper-hop queries relative to isolated-triple supervision, and does an adaptive one-hop-failure repair loop add reliable gains on top of it?
input.expected_contribution: (1) A controlled empirical comparison isolating the effect of passage-derived context triples vs. isolated triples under matched data and compute. (2) Evidence on whether context-enriched supervision transfers from shallow to deeper-hop queries. (3) A reusable adaptive repair procedure for one-hop failures and evidence on whether it improves or merely shifts errors. (4) A documented negative result if any component fails under controlled conditions.

controls: identical KG and question set (same train/dev/test split)
matched number of training examples and total supervision tokens across regimes
matched number of optimization steps and random seeds
dependent: multi-hop answer accuracy (Hits@1 for KGQA; exact match / F1 for text-form answers)
accuracy on held-out deeper-hop queries (hop-depth transfer)
fact-level correctness rate of base facts
independent: supervision regime (isolated triple/path vs. triple/path + local context subgraph)
repair loop enabled/disabled and number of repair iterations
RL stage enabled/disabled and training hop depth (e.g. 1-2 hop)

assumptions: Triples used as supervision can be linked to a source passage, so that 'co-passage triples' are well defined (this does NOT hold for pure Freebase/Wikidata-only KGQA without provenance).
Triples co-occurring in the same passage are relevant, largely non-misleading context for the target triple.
One-hop failures on the training/validation distribution are diagnostic of base-fact errors that corrective examples can reduce.
Transfer from lower-hop to higher-hop queries is measureable on a fixed KG with a fixed question vocabulary.

ambiguities.question: Which metric defines success: Hits@1 for KGQA-style evaluation, or EM/F1 for text answers?
ambiguities.resolution: Use Hits@1 for KG answer grounding and EM/F1 if answers are generated text; report both where possible. KGQA benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ, MetaQA) commonly use Hits@1, so this is resolvable from the literature.

ambiguities.question: Which datasets and knowledge graphs define the evaluation setting?
ambiguities.resolution: MetaQA (1/2/3-hop), WebQSP and CWQ are the standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks used by embedding-, path- and LLM-based methods (Saxena et al. 2020; He et al. 2021; Jiang et al. 2022; Mavromatis & Karypis 2025).

ambiguities.question: Which model is being fine-tuned — a small KGQA-specific encoder/GNN or a large decoder-only LLM?
ambiguities.resolution: Assume an instruction-tuned decoder-only LLM as the primary target system (to match the 'language-model training' framing), with a GNN/path-based KGQA model as a secondary baseline; this remains partially unresolved.

ambiguities.question: What exactly is a 'source passage' when the supervision is drawn from a structured KG rather than text?
ambiguities.resolution: Assume provenance-bearing KGs (e.g. text-derived graphs, HotpotQA-style supporting paragraphs, or KGs with sentence/paragraph provenance); if no provenance exists the mechanism is undefined and the scope must be narrowed to text-grounded KGs.

ambiguities.question: How deep is 'lower-hop' training vs. 'deeper' test (1-hop to 3-hop? 2-hop to 3-hop?)
ambiguities.resolution: Assume training on 1-2 hop instances and testing on 2-3 hop instances with a held-out hop split; exact split to be fixed during experiment planning.

ambiguities.question: What RL algorithm and reward are used in the lower-hop optimization stage?
ambiguities.resolution: Unresolved; assume a policy-gradient/GRPO-style objective with a task-accuracy (Hits@1 or EM) reward on lower-hop instances, optionally with a path-validity shaping term (cf. Lin et al. 2018).

search_queries: knowledge graph augmented language model pretraining multi-hop question answering context triples
multi-hop question answering knowledge graph reasoning path reinforcement learning
subgraph context enhanced knowledge graph embedding training beyond isolated triples
iterative self-repair error correction training examples knowledge graph question answering
MetaQA WebQSP CWQ benchmark multi-hop knowledge graph question answering evaluation
potential_risks: Passage provenance may not exist for standard Freebase/Wikidata KGQA, making the mechanism inapplicable to the strongest baselines' setting.
The context regime may be confounded with simply seeing more tokens/more triples; matched-token controls are essential and hard to satisfy.
Co-passage triples may be topical noise rather than reasoning-relevant context, so enrichment could hurt.
The adaptive repair loop may chase label noise / reward hacking and amplify rather than fix one-hop failures.
RL on lower-hop instances may overfit shallow patterns and fail to transfer, yielding a null or negative result.
Many recent LLM+RAG-over-KG systems already retrieve subgraphs per query, so the novelty of context enrichment may be limited to the training-supervision framing.

input.question: Can the context-enrichment mechanism even be instantiated on standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ), which use Freebase/Wikidata where triples lack source-passage provenance? If not, the idea's core mechanism is undefined for the strongest baselines and scope must narrow to text-grounded KGs.
input.description: The idea requires 'additional triples drawn from the same source passage'. Standard KGQA benchmarks use structured KGs without passages. Either (a) provenance-bearing text-grounded KGs must be adopted (e.g. HotpotQA supporting paragraphs, text-derived graphs), or (b) 'context' must be redefined as graph-neighborhood (k-hop around the target), which is very different and likely already explored.
input.rationale: If provenance is unavailable, the proposed mechanism cannot be evaluated against the field's standard baselines and the contribution is at risk of being untestable as stated.

input.question: Is context-subgraph supervision for triple/path training genuinely novel, or is it already covered by subgraph-based KGQA, graph-RAG, and KG-completion subgraph retrieval methods (DrKGC, GRAG, GNN-RAG, SG-RAG)?
input.description: Subgraph retrieval-augmentation is a well-populated area at inference time; the open question is whether the specific framing of enriching the TRAINING supervision signal (not just retrieval at test time) with co-passage triples is differentiated.
input.rationale: Novelty cannot be claimed until the closest subgraph-augmentation work is read and its overlap with training-time context enrichment is assessed.

input.question: Would any accuracy gain from the context regime be attributable to the context itself rather than to the model seeing more tokens/triples or more training signal per example?
input.description: The natural control is matched supervision budget: equal number of examples AND equal token budget, with the isolated regime given unrelated/random triples of the same length. Without this, gains are uninterpretable.
input.rationale: This is the single most likely way the main effect could be an artifact, and it directly determines whether the contribution is defensible.
